Components

Each page shows a component in every variant and state, with a do and a don't.

  • Accordion A set of disclosures of which one is open at a time, built on details elements that share a name. draft
  • Activity announcer The one status region of a view that tells a screen reader what an agent's run is doing: always in the page, never drawn, and written to only when the run starts, needs approval, finishes, stops or fails. draft
  • Activity feed A chronological record of what agents and people did, grouped by day, each entry with its time, its actor, a verb phrase and an optional source or excerpt. draft
  • Alert A message inside a view about the state of what the view shows. draft
  • App header The top bar of an app: the product name or the current view's title, with an optional back link, actions and a tray for approvals that are waiting. draft
  • Approval One request from an agent that waits for the reader's answer: what would run, where, for whom and why, with Allow and Decline. draft
  • Attachment chip One file or image attached to a prompt: its kind as an icon, its name, its size in words and a button that removes it. draft
  • Avatar A small square mark for a person or an agent, holding initials, an icon or an image, with the name beside it. draft
  • Badge A status in a word or two, such as a task's station. draft
  • Banner One message about the state of the whole app, across the full width under the app header. draft
  • Breadcrumb Where the current page sits in the app, as a line of links to each page above it. draft
  • Button An action the reader takes on the current view. draft
  • Button group Related buttons shown together: the actions at the end of a form, or a joined row of closely related actions. draft
  • Calendar One month as a grid of days, for picking a single day. draft
  • Card One section of a view set apart by a border or a background shift, with an optional title, one quiet action and a body. draft
  • Check list The results of the automated checks on a run: each check's name, its result in words, how long it took and, behind a disclosure, its output. draft
  • Checkbox A native checkbox with its label: one yes-or-no choice, or several independent choices in a group, sent with a form. draft
  • Code block A block of mono text for a command, a log or a program's output. draft
  • Combobox A text input that filters a list of options as the reader types, for one choice from a list too long to scan. draft
  • Command palette A modal dialog with a search input over a grouped list of commands, for running any command of the app from the keyboard. draft
  • Composer The prompt input that starts and continues work with an agent: a textarea that grows with its content and Send, optionally as one block with Add context, the model and dictation in a row under the text. draft
  • Confirm dialog A dialog that asks before something is deleted or discarded, and says in plain words what will be lost. draft
  • Context list The rows of the Add context sheet: a rounded group of buttons, each naming a setting of the next task, showing its current value and opening the setting's own view. draft
  • Context menu The actions on one row of a list or a table, in a menu opened from a More actions button at the end of the row. draft
  • Copy button A small button that copies a value shown next to it, and says in words that it did. draft
  • Copy field A read-only value the reader takes somewhere else, with a button that copies it. draft
  • Data table Things compared across columns on a real table: a caption, sortable headers, numeric columns, one action for each row, rows that expand, and a stacked layout on a phone. draft
  • Date field A native date input, or date and time input, as the control of a field, with a hint for what to enter and its earliest and latest values. draft
  • Device code What a view shows while the reader connects an outside account by entering a short code on that account's own site: the steps, the link, the code, and whether the app is still waiting. draft
  • Dialog A modal window for one short task that must be finished or cancelled before the reader goes on. draft
  • Diff One file's change as a unified diff, with its path and how many lines were added and removed. draft
  • Disclosure A native details element that shows or hides detail under a summary written in text. draft
  • Editable list An ordered list whose items the reader can edit in place, add to and delete from, such as the tasks in an agent's plan before it is approved. draft
  • Empty state What a view shows when it has no data yet, with the way to get some. draft
  • Error state What a view shows when its data could not be loaded, with a way to try again. draft
  • Feedback A control for rating an agent's answer as helpful or not helpful, with an optional follow-up note and a confirmation. draft
  • Field One labelled control, a text input, a textarea or a select, with its description and its error message. draft
  • File upload A file input drawn as a drop area with a button in it, with what it accepts in words and the chosen files listed under it. draft
  • Filter chips A row of filters the reader switches on and off above the list they narrow, built on native checkboxes or radios. draft
  • Hover card A preview of a linked item, such as a run, a branch or a person, shown beside its link so the reader can decide whether to follow it. draft
  • Icon button A button that shows only an icon, for a familiar action where a text label has no room. draft
  • Inspector A panel for the details of the item selected in the content beside it, with a title, a close button and sections of labelled values. draft
  • Jump to latest A small button that shows while the reader has scrolled up in a transcript and new rows have arrived, saying how many in words and taking them to the newest. draft
  • Kbd A keyboard key or shortcut named in text, such as Ctrl + K. draft
  • Key-value Facts about one thing as label and value pairs: stacked on a phone, in two columns at 768px and wider. draft
  • Link A text link to another view or another site: in running text, standing alone, external or quiet. draft
  • List Rows one above the other, each with a primary line and room for a second line, an icon, and trailing text or one quiet action. draft
  • Listbox A list of options, always in view, from which the reader selects one or several. draft
  • Menu A list of actions on one thing, opened from a button. draft
  • Message One row of an agent transcript: the start of the session, a prompt, the agent's text, a question to the reader, a tool call, its result, an answered permission request, a denial, an error, usage or the end of a turn. draft
  • Notification list What happened while the reader was away, grouped as unread and earlier: each entry says what happened, where and when, and offers at most one action. draft
  • Now doing One line under a transcript that says in words what the agent is doing right now and for how long, with Stop beside it, or what the run is waiting on the reader for, with a link to it. draft
  • Number field A numeric input as the control of a field, with an optional unit written beside it and optional stepper buttons. draft
  • Option picker Exactly one of up to about ten options, each a full-width row with a name, a one-line description and an optional state in words, built on native radios. draft
  • One-time-code input A single input for a short one-time code, drawn with wide letter spacing so each digit can be checked. draft
  • Page header The top of a view: its title, an optional one-line description and the view's one optional primary action. draft
  • Pagination Previous and next for a list split into pages, with the position written in words and optional numbered pages. draft
  • Password field A password input as the control of a field, with a button that shows or hides what was typed. draft
  • Pending tray How many approvals are waiting for the reader, in words and a count, linking to the queue from every screen. draft
  • Popover A small panel beside the button that opens it, for short supplementary content or a small form, which does not block the page. draft
  • Progress How far a job with a known length has got: a labelled bar on a native progress element, with the value written in words. draft
  • Radio A native radio group: exactly one of a few options, each with room for a full label and a description, sent with a form. draft
  • Reasoning A closed disclosure holding an agent's reasoning or plan notes, drawn quietly so it defers to the answer. draft
  • Run status The content of one list row that summarises a run or a task: its title, its station as a badge in words, who or what is acting and the elapsed time. draft
  • Run timeline The stations a run passes through, in order, each with its state in words: done with how long it took, running with the time so far, waiting on the owner, failed or not started. draft
  • Search field A search input with a search icon, an optional clear button and a line that counts the results. draft
  • Segmented control Two to five short options of which exactly one is chosen, shown side by side. draft
  • Select A native select as the control of a field, for one choice from a short fixed list. draft
  • Selection basket The bar that appears while rows of a list or a table are selected: how many are selected, one bulk action, a More menu and Clear selection. draft
  • Settings row One setting as a row: its label and a one-line description, with a single control or a status at the far end. draft
  • Sheet A panel for a longer form or the details of an item, rising from the bottom edge on a phone and sitting as a side panel at 768px and wider. draft
  • Show more A control after the first part of long content that reveals the rest: a details element for text, code or a log, and a quiet button for a list cut short. draft
  • Sidebar nav The destinations of an app in a column beside the content at 768px and up, each with an icon and a text label, grouped into labelled sections. draft
  • Skeleton Plain shapes that stand where content is about to appear, so the page keeps its layout while it loads. draft
  • Slider A native range input for a rough amount, with its label, its value in words and a label at each end. draft
  • Source chip A compact link to where something came from: a file with an optional line range, a web page by its host, or a commit. draft
  • Sparkline A small trend line beside a value, with words that say the trend and the latest value. draft
  • Spinner A sign that something is in progress when how long it will take is not known. draft
  • Split button A main action joined to a menu button that holds other ways to do the same thing. draft
  • Split panel Two labelled regions, a list and the detail of the row chosen in it, side by side at 768px and up and stacked below, each scrolling by itself. draft
  • Stat One number in context: a label that says what it counts, the value in tabular figures, and a line that gives its comparison, its period or its scope. draft
  • Step group A run of consecutive steps in a long turn folded under one line: counts by kind in plain words, how long they took, and any failure, running step or pending approval called out in words in the summary itself. draft
  • Stepper Where the reader is in a short, fixed sequence of named steps: which are completed, which is current and which are still to come. draft
  • Streaming The note that the agent is still producing output: a small turning mark and words that say what is happening. draft
  • Suggestion chips Two to four suggested next prompts, as quiet buttons under a composer or an empty transcript. draft
  • Switch An on-or-off setting that takes effect as soon as it changes. draft
  • Tab bar The two to five main destinations of an app, along the bottom of a phone screen, each with an icon and a text label. draft
  • Tabs A row of tabs that switches between panels of one view, showing one panel at a time. draft
  • Tag A small neutral label for a category or a filter value, with an optional remove button. draft
  • Tag input A box holding the values already added, as removable tags, and a text input for adding the next one. draft
  • Textarea The multi-line control of a field, which grows with what the reader types. draft
  • Timeline Events in the order they happened, each with its time, who acted and what happened, joined by a rail. draft
  • Toast A brief status message that appears at the edge of the screen without taking focus and leaves by itself. draft
  • Toggle button A button that turns one view option on or off, such as Wrap lines, and says which with aria-pressed. draft
  • Tool call One call a tool was asked to make, through its whole life: a line that is always in view with the status in words, a plain summary and the time, the arguments and output behind one disclosure, and Allow and Decline while it waits for approval. draft
  • Toolbar A row of related controls for one view, grouped and labelled, that wraps or scrolls on a narrow screen. draft
  • Tooltip A line of supplementary text for a control that already has a visible label or an accessible name. draft
  • Tree A file tree or an outline whose folders open and close with no script, built on nested details elements. draft
  • Undo toast A toast for an action that can be taken back: it says what happened, offers Undo and shows how long Undo stays. draft
  • Usage meter How much of a limit is used, on a native meter, with the figures and the state written in words. draft

Page patterns

Each page shows a whole screen composed from the components, in every state, with a do and a don't.

  • Agent run The screen of one agent run inside the app shell: the run's title and its stations at the top, the transcript as a log of messages and step groups, and a dock at the bottom with the jump-to-latest control, the now-doing line and the composer. draft
  • App shell The frame of a signed-in screen: the app header with the pending tray, the sidebar nav from 768px and the tab bar below it, and a main column that starts with the view's page header. draft
  • Filter and results A screen that narrows a long list or table: a search field and a few filters above it, the filters in force as removable tags, a count in words, then the results. draft
  • Master and detail A screen with a list of items and the selected item's detail: side by side from 768px, and on a phone the list alone, with the detail as a view of its own. draft
  • Multi-step form A longer task split into steps shown one at a time: which step this is in words, the step's fields, Back and one primary action, and a review step before the final action. draft
  • Not found The screen for a missing page or a missing item: what was not found in plain words, why that might be, one primary way forward and a quiet second link. draft
  • Settings page A screen of settings shown defaults first: the few settings most people change, one advanced disclosure holding the rest, and a marked danger area for actions that destroy something. draft
  • Sign in The sign-in screen: the product's name, one sentence, the fields, one primary action and a quiet link for trouble signing in, in a reading-width column at the leading edge. draft
